words.note: Refers to emotional or romantic love. Sounds formal or literary; in daily life, すき (suki) is more common for 'like/love'.

dictionary.kana: かぞくのあいはつよい。

words.note: Polite way to say 'no'. Placed at the start of a sentence (いいえ、〜) to soften disagreement or refusal. Casual speech uses ううん (uun).
Means 'up' or 'above'. Often used with the particle の to say something is on top of another object (つくえのうえ). Opposite is した (shita).

dictionary.kana: ほんがつくえのうえにある。
dictionary.romaji: hon ga tsukue no ue ni aru
dictionary.english: A book is on the desk.

words.note: Neutral word for 'house' or 'home'. The more casual うち (uchi) refers to one’s own home or family.

dictionary.kana: いえでべんきょうする。

words.note: い-adjective meaning 'blue'. Historically covered both blue and green shades. The noun form is あお (ao).

dictionary.kana: あおいくるまがすきだ。

words.note: Means 'to meet' or 'to see (a person)'. Usually takes the particle に to mark who you meet.
A very common motion verb used with the particle に to indicate destination. Irregular past tense: いった (itta).
A versatile verb meaning both 'to listen' (音楽をきく) and 'to ask' (先生にきく). The meaning depends on the particle used.
A basic transitive verb meaning 'to buy'. Often used with を to mark the purchased item.
Means the physical 'face'. Used in many set phrases like かおをあらう (wash face) or かおがひろい (well-connected person).
Usually refers to small, man-made ponds found in parks or gardens. Natural ponds may also be called ぬま (numa).

dictionary.english: There are fish in the pond.

words.note: Refers to human or animal voices (not mechanical sounds). For mechanical noises, use おと (oto).

dictionary.english: to speak in a loud voice

words.note: Common everyday word meaning 'movie'. Often paired with みる (to watch).

dictionary.kana: えいがについてはなす。

words.note: Literally 'outside country'. Used for any country other than Japan. Appears in words like がいこくじん (foreigner).

dictionary.kana: がいこくのえいがをみる。

words.note: Used for the time period after noon. Usually appears before a time (ごごさんじ – 3 PM).

dictionary.kana: ごごにべんきょうする。

words.note: Means 'key' for locks or doors. Can also mean 'hint' or 'clue' in abstract phrases (しあいのかぎ – 'key to the match').
A general term for household furniture. Often appears in compounds like でんきかぐ (electrical appliances).

dictionary.english: There is furniture in the room.

words.note: Used for both physical shadows and metaphorical ones (like かげで meaning 'behind the scenes').

dictionary.english: to rest in the shade of a tree

words.note: Japan’s most famous flower, symbolizing spring and renewal. Often seen in festivals and poetry.

dictionary.kana: さくらのきのしたをあるく。
dictionary.romaji: sakura no ki no shita wo aruku
dictionary.english: to walk under the cherry trees

words.note: Basic seasoning used in cooking. Often written with kanji 塩.
Describes where someone lives. Always used with the particle に (e.g., 東京にすむ).
Means 'seat' or 'assigned place'. Also used for 'cough' (different kanji). Context clarifies the meaning.

dictionary.english: to stand up from a seat

words.note: Common word for the sky or heavens. Used in expressions like そらをみる (to look at the sky).

dictionary.english: a bird flies in the sky

words.note: Demonstrative adjective meaning 'that (near listener)'. Used before nouns, like そのほん ('that book').
Refers to a bamboo strainer or colander, common in Japanese kitchens. Appears in ざるそば (cold soba dish).

dictionary.kana: ざるにやさいをいれる。
dictionary.english: to put vegetables in a strainer

words.note: A book or digital tool for looking up words. Often used with the verb つかう (to use).

dictionary.kana: じしょでことばをさがす。
dictionary.english: to look up a word in a dictionary

dictionary.kana: あたらしいじしょをかう。

words.note: Used for diagrams, figures, or drawings (e.g., 地図 – 'map'). Appears in compound words like 図書館 (library).

dictionary.english: to draw a figure on a map

words.note: Common noun meaning 'tax'. Seen in compounds like ぜいきん (tax money) and ぜいぬき (before tax).
Common animal word for 'elephant'. Used in expressions like ぞうのはな (elephant’s trunk).

dictionary.kana: どうぶつえんにぞうがいる。
dictionary.english: there is an elephant in the zoo

words.note: Means 'accident', commonly used for traffic accidents (こうつうじこ).
Very common ichidan verb meaning 'to eat'. Takes を for the object. Polite form: たべます.
Means 'map'. Written 地図. Common in travel or direction contexts.

dictionary.kana: ちずでばしょをさがす。
dictionary.english: to find a place on a map

words.note: Means both 'moon' and 'month'. Written 月. Polite expressions use です naturally.
Means a handwritten letter. Written 手紙. Often used with かく (to write).
General word for 'friend'. Can be shortened to とも casually. です used only when introducing politely.

polite.kana: ともだちとあそびます。

words.note: Means both 'clock' and 'watch'. Written 時計. です used naturally in polite introductions.
Means 'train'. Written 電車. Common in travel and commuting contexts.
Means 'university' or 'college'. Written 大学. です used naturally in self-introductions.

dictionary.kana: だいがくでべんきょうする。

words.note: Expresses ability or possibility. Often used with が (日本語ができる). Polite form: できます.
Loanword from English 'door', written ドア. Can take polite です when identifying.
Common question word meaning 'who'. Appears naturally inside polite questions (〜ですか).
Loanword from 'department store', written デパート. Common shopping term.

dictionary.kana: でぱーとでかいものをする。
dictionary.english: to shop at a department store
to go to a department store

polite.kana: でぱーとでかいものをします。
polite.english: I shop at a department store.
I go to a department store.

words.note: Common word for someone's name. Often asked politely as おなまえは？ ('What is your name?').
General word for meat. Often specified as とりにく (chicken) or ぶたにく (pork).
Basic word for 'cat'. Often appears with すきです ('I like ...').
Common question word meaning 'what'. Changes to なん before certain sounds (e.g., なんですか).
Season word for 'summer'. Common in greetings like なつやすみ (summer vacation).

past.kana: なつがあつかったです。

words.note: Means 'inside' or 'middle'. Often used with の: はこのなか (inside the box).
Can mean 'flower' (花) or 'nose' (鼻) depending on context.
Basic word for 'person'. Written 人. Often used with adjectives like しんせつな (kind).
Common word for 'boat' or 'ship'. Written 船. Frequently pairs with のる (ride).

polite.kana: ふねがうみをわたります。

words.note: Often used with が to describe a lack of ability. Polite forms take です／でした.
Common word for 'star'. Written 星. Appears in phrases like ほしをみる (to look at the stars).

dictionary.english: There are stars in the sky.

polite.kana: そらにほしがあります。
polite.english: There are stars in the sky.

words.note: Humble word for 'my mother'. Written 母. For someone else’s mother, use おかあさん.

past.kana: ははのりょうりでした。

words.note: Common everyday word meaning 'fool' or 'stupid'. Can sound rude depending on context. Written 馬鹿.
Means 'beautiful woman'. Uses じ from the Z-row. Written 美人.

polite.kana: かのじょはびじんです。

past.kana: かのじょはびじんでした。

words.note: Common farm animal. Written 豚. Also appears in words like ぶたにく (pork).
Means 'separate' or 'different'. Common in べつべつ (separately). Written 別.
Common everyday item meaning 'hat' or 'cap'. Written 帽子.

past.kana: ぼうしをかぶりました。

words.note: Used to express multiples (e.g., twice = にばい). Written 倍.
Very common everyday word meaning 'full' or 'a lot'. Written 一杯.

dictionary.kana: おちゃがいっぱいある。

polite.english: There is a lot of water.

polite.kana: おちゃがいっぱいあります。

past.kana: みずがいっぱいでした。

words.note: Means 'leaf' (of a plant/tree). Written 葉っぱ. Doubled consonant adds natural sound emphasis.
Mimetic word describing something shiny or sparkling. Common with です／でした.

polite.kana: くるまがぴかぴかです。

past.kana: くるまがぴかぴかでした。

words.note: Mimetic word often used for language fluency. Written ペラペラ.

polite.kana: にほんごがぺらぺらです。

past.kana: にほんごがぺらぺらでした。

words.note: Mimetic word describing gentle warmth, like spring sunlight. Written ポカポカ.

past.kana: へやがぽかぽかでした。

words.note: Mimetic word describing a flapping or pattering sound. Often paired with と (onomatopoeic particle).

dictionary.kana: とりがぱたぱたととぶ。

polite.kana: とりがぱたぱたととびます。

past.kana: とりがぱたぱたととびました。

words.note: Essential everyday word. Written 水. Often used with のむ (to drink).
Common word for town or city. Written 町.
Basic word for 'ear'. Written 耳. Appears in phrases with きく (to listen).

dictionary.english: to hear a sound with your ear.

polite.kana: みみでおとをききます。
polite.english: I hear a sound with my ear.

past.kana: みみでおとをききました。
past.english: I heard a sound with my ear.

words.note: Common everyday word. Written 虫.
Common word for eyeglasses. Written 眼鏡. Often used with かける (to wear).
Common fruit. Written 桃. Often appears in phrases like ももをたべる.
Common everyday word meaning 'mountain'. Written 山.
Common food category word. Written 野菜. Often used with たべる (to eat).
Very common seasonal word. Written 雪. Often used with ふる (to fall).
Basic body part word meaning 'finger'. Written 指. Often used with さす (to point).
Common abstract noun meaning 'dream'. Written 夢. Appears with みる (to see/dream).
Common word for 'side' or 'beside'. Written 横. Often used with の.
Common school subject word. Written 歴史 in kanji.
Used when someone is away from home. Written 留守 in kanji.
Used in phrases like らくな (easy/comfortable). Written 楽 in kanji.
Animal word. Written 栗鼠 in kanji (rare).
Common school and building word. Written 廊下 in kanji.
Everyday object word. Written 喇叭 in kanji (rare, often kana). Uses small っ.
Common animal word. Written 鰐 in kanji.

example.english: the crocodile is in the river

words.note: Common first-person pronoun. Written 私 in kanji.

example.kana: わたしはがくせいです

words.note: Basic everyday noun. Written 本 in kanji.
Common abstract noun. Written 音楽 in kanji.
Common noun for teacher/doctor/master. Written 先生 in kanji.

example.kana: せんせいはやさしいです

words.note: Everyday word for telephone. Written 電話 in kanji.
